about: Despite its place among the ryes, this is a bourbon, and the Springbrook whiskey most closely tied to the farm. Springbrook Hollow Farm Distillery was founded in 2014 by Dave Bannon and four friends on his former horse farm near Lake George, in the foothills of the Adirondacks. Its Adirondack whiskeys are named for those mountains, and the distillery draws its water from the Springbrook Hollow spring that gives it its name.

Adirondack High Rye is made from local corn, rye and malted barley, with a larger share of rye than a typical bourbon carries, and aged in heavy-char new oak barrels; Springbrook’s barrels come from Adirondack Barrel Cooperage in Utica. Early releases were bottled at two years old, while more recent accounts describe four years in barrel. It is bottled at 43% alcohol, or 86 proof.

The distillery suggests it in a Manhattan, an Old Fashioned or neat, and describes caramel and vanilla on the nose, oak and toffee on the palate and a spicy lift from the rye. Wine Enthusiast’s Kara Newman found it light and fresh, with almond, vanilla, baking spice and a brief note of baked pear. It won Silver, with 88 points, at the 2025 Bartender Spirits Awards.
